beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:wonder, naming the giants][tune:level]Mammoths. [act:same rhythm][tune:level]Mastodons. [act:delighted, a little bigger][tune:fall]Ground sloths the size of a ^car. [act:setting the scene, vivid]Giants once roamed the Ice Age world, from the Americas to ^Australia. [act:slowing down][tune:level]Then... [act:quiet, final][tune:highfall]^*gone*.
[d:tension][act:posing the big question, intrigued][tune:rise]Did ^one blow from the ^sky kill them all?

[d:calm][act:plain, sober facts]North America alone lost about ^thirty-five kinds of large animal: horses, camels, sabre-toothed cats, giant ^beavers. [p:0.93][act:curious, the method]How do we know ^when? [act:explaining, an everyday picture]Bones carry a faint natural radioactivity that fades after death at a steady pace, like a candle burning ^down. [act:precise, unhurried]The youngest bones of each kind cluster between ^thirteen thousand eight hundred and ^eleven thousand four hundred years ago.

[d:build][go:2|0][sfx:shimmer][act:intrigued, a clue]And at many sites, a dark layer, the ^black mat, about twelve thousand nine hundred years old, lies right on ^top of the last mammoth bones. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a picture]Layers pile up like ^pages, so what lies just above the bones came just ^after them.

[d:build][act:the turn, widening the view][tune:fall]But zoom ^out, to the whole world. [p:0.93][act:explaining, the logic]If one blow from the sky had done it, giants everywhere should vanish at the same ^moment. [act:counting them off, brisk][tune:level]^Australia's giants went about ^forty-six thousand years ago. [act:continuing, same pace][tune:level]The woolly ^rhino, about ^fourteen thousand. [act:the surprise, a touch slower][tune:fall]And the giant ^deer lived on to ^seven thousand seven hundred.

[d:build][act:wonder, a remarkable fact]And on an island in the ^Arctic, [count:4,000|years ago]mammoths survived until about ^four thousand years ago. [d:aside][act:playful, lighter]By then, the ^pyramids of Egypt were ^already standing. [act:mischievous, childlike delight][tune:fall]Somewhere, a mammoth could have watched the ^news.

[d:reveal][act:the reveal, clear and deliberate]So the deaths were ^staggered, continent by continent, [sfx:hit]and they tend to follow two things. [act:explaining, the first][tune:level]The arrival of ^people: where people spread, the giants tended to vanish soon ^after. [act:explaining, the second][tune:fall]And the wild ^climate swings of the melt, as the Ice Age lurched between cold and ^warm.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]A ^single cataclysm? [act:the verdict, firm][tune:fall]*Ruled ^out* by the dates. [act:even, open-handed][tune:fall]^Hunting, ^climate, or ^both? [act:honest, level-headed][tune:fall]Still ^argued.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:quiet, certain][tune:fall]The giants didn't fall in ^one night. [act:the last word, slow and weighty][tune:fall]They fell over ^*forty thousand years*.
